s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal syndrome with chronic abdominal pain and vomiting, featuring a tender abdominal mass
salient_findings: Large, firm, tender mass near the umbilicus
Diffuse lymphadenopathy and mesenteric mass on CT
key_facts: Normal passage of stool and flatus
Large, firm, tender mass near the umbilicus
Low bicarbonate, low PCO2, marginally acidotic pH on venous blood gas
No evidence of infection on urinalysis and blood cultures
CT Abdomen findings: Diffuse lymphadenopathy and a large mesenteric mass
Mesenteric mass abutting multiple segments of small intestine and encasing the mesenteric vasculature

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse lymphadenopathy and a large mesenteric mass on CT Abdomen

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Large mesenteric mass abutting multiple segments of small intestine

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Large, firm, tender mass near the umbilicus and mesenteric mass on CT Abdomen

shortlist.label: Carcinoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic abdominal pain and vomiting with a tender abdominal mass

shortlist.label: Metastatic cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Large mesenteric mass and diffuse lymphadenopathy, suggesting possible metastasis

raw.rationale: The presence of diffuse lymphadenopathy and a large mesenteric mass on CT Abdomen, along with the patient's symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, are consistent with lymphoma. The elevated lactate levels and acidotic pH also suggest possible bowel ischemia due to the mesenteric mass encasing the mesenteric vasculature, which can be seen in lymphoma.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of diffuse lymphadenopathy is more suggestive of lymphoma than a gastrointestinal stromal tumor.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: Desmoid tumors are typically associated with a history of familial adenomatous polyposis or previous abdominal surgery, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Carcinoid tumor
rejected.why: Carcinoid tumors often present with flushing, diarrhea, and wheezing, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Metastatic cancer
rejected.why: While metastatic cancer is possible, the presence of diffuse lymphadenopathy and a large mesenteric mass without a known primary cancer makes lymphoma a more likely diagnosis.
